_link.title: I can calculate the magnetic force on a moving charged particle using F = qvB

toLevel2.stem: Which formula gives the magnetic force on a charged particle moving perpendicular to a magnetic field?
distractors: F = qE
F = BIl
F = mv²/r

toLevel2.stem: In the formula F = qvB, what does the variable q represent?
toLevel2.answer: The charge of the particle in coulombs
distractors: The mass of the particle in kilograms
The speed of the particle in metres per second
The strength of the field in tesla units

toLevel2.stem: What is the SI unit of charge used in the formula F = qvB?
distractors: Ampere (A)
Volt (V)
Tesla (T)

toLevel2.stem: An electron with charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C moves at 1.0 × 10⁶ m/s through a 0.10 T field. What is the force on the electron?
When does the formula F = qvB apply to a charged particle in a magnetic field?
toLevel2.answer: When the velocity is perpendicular to the field
distractors: When the velocity is parallel to the field
When the particle is stationary in the field
When the particle has no electric charge at all

toLevel2.stem: The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by F = {{blank:1}}, where v is the {{blank:2}} of the particle.
A charged particle must be {{blank:1}} to experience a magnetic force, and the force is zero when the particle moves {{blank:2}} to the field.
In F = qvB, B is measured in {{blank:1}} and F is measured in {{blank:2}}.
A stationary charged particle in a magnetic field experiences a magnetic force.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: The magnetic force on a moving charged particle depends on the particle's speed.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Why does a charged particle experience no magnetic force when moving parallel to the field?
toLevel3.answer: The force depends on the component of velocity perpendicular to the field, which is zero when parallel
distractors: The magnetic field cancels out when the particle moves in the same direction as the field
The charge of the particle drops to zero when its velocity is aligned with the field lines
The particle's speed decreases to zero when it moves parallel to the magnetic field lines

toLevel3.stem: A proton and an electron move at the same speed through the same magnetic field. How do the magnitudes of the forces on them compare?
toLevel3.answer: The forces are equal in magnitude because both particles have the same charge magnitude
distractors: The force on the proton is larger because the proton has a much greater mass value
The force on the electron is larger because electrons interact more strongly with fields
The forces cannot be compared because protons and electrons have opposite charge signs

toLevel3.stem: Why does the magnetic force on a charged particle not do work on the particle?
toLevel3.answer: The force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it changes direction but not speed
distractors: The force is too small to have any measurable effect on the particle's kinetic energy
The magnetic field absorbs the energy that would otherwise be transferred to the particle
The force acts parallel to the velocity and therefore only increases the particle's speed

toLevel3.stem: A particle with charge 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C moves at 5.0 × 10⁵ m/s in a 0.040 T field. What force does it experience?
If the speed of a charged particle is doubled while the field strength remains constant, what happens to the magnetic force?
distractors: The force quadruples
The force is halved
The force stays the same

toLevel3.stem: Why does a neutral atom moving through a magnetic field experience no net magnetic force?
toLevel3.answer: Its net charge is zero, so F = qvB gives zero force
distractors: Neutral atoms cannot move fast enough to experience any magnetic effects at all
The magnetic field passes through neutral atoms without any interaction occurring
Neutral atoms are too large for the magnetic field to exert a force on their surface

toLevel3.stem: The magnetic force is always {{blank:1}} to the velocity, so it changes the particle's {{blank:2}} but not its speed.
Doubling the {{blank:1}} of a particle doubles the magnetic force, while doubling its {{blank:2}} has no effect on the force.
Because the magnetic force does no {{blank:1}} on the particle, the particle's kinetic {{blank:2}} remains constant.
A proton and an electron moving at the same speed in the same field experience forces of the same magnitude.
distractors: False

toLevel4.stem: An alpha particle (q = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 1.5 × 10⁷ m/s through a 0.50 T field perpendicular to its velocity. What is the magnetic force?
A charged particle enters a magnetic field at 45° to the field lines. How does the force compare to the case when it enters perpendicularly?
toLevel4.answer: The force is smaller because only the perpendicular component of velocity contributes
distractors: The force is the same because the total speed is unchanged regardless of the angle
The force is larger because the particle spends more time interacting with the field
The force is zero because the particle must be exactly perpendicular to experience force

toLevel4.stem: An electron experiences a force of 8.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ N in a 0.25 T field. What is the electron's speed?
A proton (q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) must experience a force of at least 1.0 × 10⁻¹² N in a 0.40 T field. What minimum speed is required?
Two particles with the same charge enter the same field at the same speed, but particle X moves perpendicular to the field and particle Y moves at 30° to the field. Compare their forces.
toLevel4.answer: Particle X experiences twice the force of particle Y
distractors: Both particles experience exactly the same magnetic force value
Particle Y experiences twice the force of particle X in this situation
Particle Y experiences no force because it is not exactly perpendicular

toLevel4.stem: A doubly charged ion (q = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) and a singly charged ion (q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) move at the same speed in the same field. How do their forces compare?
toLevel4.answer: The doubly charged ion experiences twice the force
distractors: Both ions experience exactly the same force value
The singly charged ion experiences twice the force
The doubly charged ion experiences four times force

toLevel4.stem: A particle moves through a region where both electric and magnetic fields are present. The particle moves in a straight line at constant speed. What can be concluded?
toLevel4.answer: The electric and magnetic forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
distractors: There is no magnetic force acting on the particle in this particular region at all
The electric field is zero and only the magnetic field is acting on the particle here
The particle has no charge and therefore neither field exerts any force on the particle

toLevel4.stem: An electron moving at 3.0 × 10⁶ m/s in a 0.050 T field experiences a force of {{blank:1}} × 10⁻¹⁴ N, directed {{blank:2}} to both the velocity and the field.
When a particle enters a field at an angle, only the {{blank:1}} component of velocity contributes to the force, reducing the force by a factor of {{blank:2}} of the angle.
To find the speed of a charged particle from its force and field strength, rearrange to v = {{blank:1}} / ({{blank:2}}).

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that since F = qvB and F = ma, doubling the speed doubles both the force and the acceleration. Evaluate whether the acceleration truly doubles.
toLevel5.answer: The acceleration doubles because the mass is unchanged and the force doubles with speed
distractors: The acceleration does not change because the particle compensates by increasing its mass
The acceleration quadruples because both force and velocity increase simultaneously
The acceleration halves because higher speed means the force acts for a shorter time

toLevel5.stem: Compare the magnetic force formula for a current-carrying wire (F = BIl) with the force on a single particle (F = qvB). Explain how they are related.
toLevel5.answer: Current is moving charges per second, so BIl represents the total force on all moving charges in the wire
distractors: The two formulas are unrelated because wires and particles obey completely different physics
The wire formula gives force per charge while the particle formula gives the total force
The wire formula applies to static charges while the particle formula applies to moving ones

toLevel5.stem: At relativistic speeds (close to the speed of light), the mass of a particle effectively increases. Predict how this affects the force calculation using F = qvB.
toLevel5.answer: The force calculation F = qvB is unchanged because it depends on charge, speed, and field, not mass
distractors: The force decreases because the increased mass reduces the effective charge of the particle
The force increases because relativistic mass makes the particle interact more with the field
The formula breaks down completely and cannot be used at any relativistic speed whatsoever

toLevel5.stem: An engineer needs to deflect a beam of protons using a magnetic field. Analyse which approach is more practical: increasing the field strength by 50% or slowing the protons by 50%.
toLevel5.answer: Both reduce or increase the force by the same factor, but slowing the protons changes their energy which may be undesirable
distractors: Slowing the protons is always better because slower particles are easier to deflect at all times
Increasing the field is always better because field strength has a squared effect on the force
Both approaches are identical in all respects because force depends on the product of v and B

toLevel5.stem: A charged particle moves through a uniform magnetic field with a velocity that has both perpendicular and parallel components. Describe the resulting path.
toLevel5.answer: The particle follows a helical path, circling due to the perpendicular component and drifting along the field
distractors: The particle follows a straight line because the parallel component cancels the circular motion
The particle spirals inward to the centre of the field and eventually comes to a complete stop
The particle follows a parabolic path similar to a projectile under gravitational influence

toLevel5.stem: Evaluate why the magnetic force cannot be used to accelerate a charged particle to higher speeds.
toLevel5.answer: The force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it can only change direction, not speed
distractors: The magnetic force is too weak to overcome the inertia of any charged particle at all
The magnetic force acts in the same direction as the velocity and therefore only maintains speed
The magnetic field absorbs kinetic energy from the particle preventing any further acceleration

toLevel5.stem: Two particles with the same kinetic energy enter the same magnetic field. Particle A has twice the mass and half the charge of Particle B. Compare the forces on them.
toLevel5.answer: Particle B experiences a greater force because it has higher charge and higher speed for the same kinetic energy
distractors: Particle A experiences a greater force because its larger mass gives it more momentum in field
Both particles experience the same force because they have the same kinetic energy value
Particle A experiences a greater force because heavier particles interact more with fields

toLevel5.stem: Analyse why cosmic rays (high-energy charged particles) from the Sun are deflected more effectively by Earth's magnetic field near the poles than at the equator.
toLevel5.answer: Near the poles the particles move more perpendicular to the field lines, increasing the magnetic force component
distractors: The magnetic field is weaker near the poles so particles are deflected into the atmosphere more
Near the poles the particles move parallel to the field lines which maximises their deflection
The atmosphere is thinner at the poles which allows the magnetic field to act more strongly

toLevel5.stem: The magnetic force cannot change a particle's {{blank:1}} because the force is always {{blank:2}} to the velocity.
When a particle has both parallel and perpendicular velocity components in a field, it follows a {{blank:1}} path, combining circular motion with {{blank:2}} drift.
